channel.title: On the Shores of Paradise
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "On the Shores of Paradise" - If we found Paradise, what would we do? Can we be sure it even is Paradise?

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded: Placeholder! Got summoned via PM to take a look-see. Will crit in a bit.

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
So I had an idea if I'm going to make this a part of the Competitive Eschatology. I've also decided to focus on a couple of protagonists here (through transcripts and emails, as both of them are high-ranking members of the ethics committee).

+ Open Protagonists
- Close Protagonsists

Both protagonists are close friends, but here is where their opinions split. This will act as the turning point that fractures their relationship.

Protagonist 1 - For evacuating people into Paradise
Has lost many people to the calamity that is Competitive Eschatology, including close friends and family members. Wants to see a bright future where no one has to suffer any more, and sees Paradise as a way to embody that future for everyone. Argues that Paradise seems completely harmless and is in fact beneficial for us. Ends up going into Paradise after a last, emotional goodbye to their friend.

Protagonist 2 - Against evacuating people into Paradise
Has also lost people to Competitive Eschatology, including family and close friends. Wants to stop the suffering all over the world, but doesn't want to use anomalies out of distrust. Argues that 'Paradise' is incredibly suspicious in how it seems to be constructed for our desires. Ends up seeing their friend off into Paradise, but not entering it themselves.

+ Open Big Reveal
- Close Big Reveal

Big argument between everyone (Ethics Committee [the protagonists], 05 Council, etc.) on whether the use of this is ethically acceptable. Eventually, increasing pressure makes the Foundation use Paradise to evacuate a whole bunch of civilians (Veil be damned) and some scientists and members of the Foundation. Once the last person comes through (one of the protagonists), all of the wildlife goes quiet, the weather stops and becomes neutral rather than perfect, and the protagonist in Paradise walks on while the protagonist seeing their friend off realises something bad is happening and tries to leap into Paradise to save their friend. They don't make it in time.

An omnipresent voice speaks out, saying 'thank you for the sacrifices', and shuts the gate, before all hell breaks loose on the beach (the animals change, the fungi and plants begin spreading, the weather changes). The protagonist outside Paradise has most of their dominant arm cut off, and is left on the beach.

The beach changes into a hostile landscape inhabited by dangerous flora and fauna that quickly begin spreading, converting all the land they spread across into more of what is at the beach (foggy and misty, cold, numerous symbols everywhere on the plants, animals, and land).

While the protagonist is dying on the beach watching everything around them turn horrible, another entity appears on the beach. They have a brief conversation where the entity introduces itself as a primordial nature spirit attracted by the happenings on Earth as a means to gain power through sacrifices. The protagonist is understandably extremely angry, but the entity says that they won't be angry for much longer and walks off. Here, the protagonist dies.

There is then an updated version of the document that reflects the recent changes that occurred, along with updates on what is going on.

To sum up the big reveal, the entity used the Paradise gateway as a means to get a bunch of sacrifices to increase its power (and harvest more sacrifices). It wants to spread itself as far as possible, and once it gets the sacrifices it uses them to change the beach into basically a spreading land virus that converts the land it touches into more of the spirit's domain to get even more sacrifices through victims.

Dunno if it's cliche or not, but I thought it fit the theme of Competitive Eschatology (specifically 'awakening'). Hope this is satisfactory!

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
The introduction of imminent conflict is definitely an improvement since it forces the Foundation to act in uncharacteristic ways and draws readers in the see the conclusion. My main question now becomes how you're going to execute this new vision: the Foundation grappling with this limited space problem but not immediately investing on the face of it, given how… "constructed" the whole thing feels.

Are you going to focus on the lore of garden, or look at a couple characters with different takes on the situation, or drop into the story in a manner akin to SCP-4646?

If you want my take, I suggest you set up a fleshed-out protagonist and antagonist to argue over the space problem, weaving that into a more general exploration of Paradise's lore, and then end with a type of subversion or reveal.

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
You make good points here, which I'll try to address (again):

+ Open
- Close

I don't think this fundamentally addresses the critique that I was giving, that the Foundation wouldn't be uniquely challenged by this.

So I have a possible solution for this, if we bring back the concept of limited space:
Have this SCP is set either in a canon where the world is becoming uninhabitable (e.g End of Death, Competitive Eschatology, Ad Astra Per Aspera, etc.), or have there be an impeding or current disaster of some sort when this SCP is discovered (or after it is discovered). With the limited space problem coupled with the problems humanity is facing, this SCP could function as an escape but also an ethical dilemma (who's staying and who's going?). As such, the Foundation must undergo serious thinking over whether the use of this at all is ethical, as it would mean leaving people behind.

If all they've got is a compulsive voice in their heads telling them it's Paradise, but people don't leave, then they'd contain it and that's the end of the story. Additionally, how is it paradise if people can't leave? Seems like a property you're just adding to make things more difficult.
I would recommend against that. A sort of "info drop" like that is something I've only ever seen work in SCP-5471. Is there a reason you can't just have the Foundation infer everything via experimentation?

Good points again. I think I'll remove that property, as it's kind of janky in regards to the anomaly (just functions as some barrier to make things more difficult, as you said).
I'll also remove the 'info drop' part of it, instead making it able to be freely explored (basically, it's a larger version of the beach, but with a couple of different biomes). It's quite small though, and there'll probably be some sort of 'end' to the pocket dimension.

That's about it for the second round of responses. Hopefully they're adequate!

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
You bring up some good points here which I'll address down below. But first, to clarify the parameters of 'Paradise':
A place free of suffering and pain. Long life is all but guaranteed and there are no responsibilities (everything we need, like technology and infrastructure) is already there. This is a permanent decision though, as you can't get back through the gateway once you enter.
Am considering whether or not this could be parallel Earth opened by people seeking a better life, or a trick by another anomaly to gather humans for food or something else.

+ Open Responses? +
- Close -

Point 1 - No Ethical Dilemma nor Containment Issues:

Ok, but how about this:
Paradise is open, free, and able to fit everyone. However, the Foundation, naturally doubtful about an offer that seems to good to be true, don't know whether this is actually Paradise or not. Thus, the Ethics Committee has a dilemma: to send everyone in there or not? By choosing to send people, the Foundation is either freeing the human race from suffering and pain forever, or sentencing them to death or something worse. Neither can be confirmed, as all technology malfunctions and stops working once it enters the gateway, and people don't come back.

Containment is marginally less important, as all the Foundation must do is bar off the area and do what they usually do, prevent any information about the place getting out.

Point 2 - Out-of-place Elements:

I am considering replacing the guardian with a memetic effect, that being that anyone who sees the gateway instantly knows what lies behind it (Paradise and the properties thereof). I hesitate because this may be viewed as cliche by other members of this Site, what do you think?

The fake iteration was placed for an in-Foundation-universe reason, namely, to act as a decoy and deter anyone trying to poke into places they weren't supposed to. However, it could simply be rendered obsolete by a warning at the top of the document that promises severe consequences for anyone accessing it without proper authorisation, as well as a memetic kill agent for additional protection.

Point 3 - Discovery:

So I was thinking about this one for a while, and I came up with this.
Very small coastal town somewhere (information would be redacted of course), close to a small beach. Paradise gateway appears, changes the beach entirely. A couple of people visit, are amazed, see the Paradise gateway and promptly enter it.
The Foundation gets strange missing person reports from that town as well as sightings of flora and fauna never seen before on Earth and decides to investigate. They find the beach and the Paradise gateway, make up explanations for the missing people, amnesticize the population of what they saw recently, and cordon off the area for 'dangerous animals' or something similar.
Does that work?

- Close -

Anyway, that's about it for my responses. Thank you for this crit, and hopefully what I've come up with is a suitable explanation for your concerns!

P.S My gratitude for you coming to crit me right after being sick for a while

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM.

I'm not sure I'm really tracking with the ethical dilemma you're presenting here. It's a paradisal pocket dimension with limited space, and that presents a problem to the Foundation why? Ideal tourist locations and life-saving medical care already exist in the real world and there isn't a mass panic over their artificial scarcity, mostly because access to those resources are controlled — the same thing the Foundation would do. I'm just not seeing why this circumstance is particularly challenging to the Foundation when their modus operandi is hiding supernatural objects, which are sometimes beneficial, to prevent mass panic.

Additionally you've got a couple elements here that seem… out of place. I'm not sure what the character of the guardian brings to this story, nor what information they could relay that isn't apparent. Likewise with the initial fake iteration, when there doesn't seem to be any interesting information presented.

Lastly regarding the discovery — generally you should try to shy away from anomalies being found in the tall grass, as it were, unless there's some deeper story reason why the Foundation specifically came across this.

item.title: Re: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
Honestly, I'm pretty down for this idea, but you're gonna actually have to choose one of your three potential paths.

I'll briefly touch on all three.

+Yeet
-Yeet

1.) This one intrigues me the most. It's a thing that is good, wholly good and purely beneficial. The catch? There's only so much room and if enough people find out and want in, people are likely gonna have to try to fight their way in, or try to force their way in somehow, staining and tainting this paradise with human greed. It's not even a Series 1 style compulsion effect, it's just people being people and being selfish because people want good things.

2.) This one kinda bores me. Very tropey, 'yeah, good stuff, we promise!' with an evil villain mustache twirl. It could work wonderfully with good execution, but eh.

3.) The third one is just a different version of 2. A tropey, 'yeah, good stuff, we promise, it's just that it's good for us and not you, never said it was good for you!' This can also work with good execution, but the simple existence of a paradise that humans greedily flock towards interests me most.

But that's just me.

I recommend reaching out to some reviewers on the butterfly squad for some more insight.

I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day, partner.

👍

item.title: On the Shores of Paradise
item.content:encoded:
Just an idea I thought of one day while asking myself a question: How would the Foundation react if there was a way to escape the Earth and the myriad of anomalies it holds? This is the result.
EDIT: Chose a path. Updated Accordingly. Thanks Quadraginta for the advice!
EDIT II: Redid my idea a bit in response to crit. Thanks Nagiros for the advice!
EDIT III: Adding in what is contained within my third response from Nagiros due to positive feedback via PM (they currently have IRL commitments, and thus can't continue the crit)

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Sorrowful, Dramatic, and Emotional (with undertones of Mystery)

Page Layout: Standard format (with ACS)

Elevator Pitch: What if there was a gateway to Paradise that we could reach? What if the entry was free? What if only the Foundation knew about it?

Here are the Shores of Paradise, a temperate, peaceful beach full of docile fauna, beautiful flora, and a gateway to Paradise. This 'Paradise' is a small pocket dimension with similar features to the beach, except with multiple biomes. As a secondary effect, the whole thing exudes a calming aura that makes people more agreeable and kinder (stronger in the pocket dimension). Sounds great, and the entry's free! But what if people found out?

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Very small coastal town somewhere close to a small beach where the Paradise gateway appears, changes the beach entirely. A couple of people visit, are amazed, see the Paradise gateway and promptly enter it.
The Foundation gets strange missing person reports from that town as well as sightings of flora and fauna never seen before on Earth and decides to investigate. They find the beach and the Paradise gateway, make up explanations for the missing people, amnesticize the population of what they saw recently, and cordon off the area for 'dangerous animals' or something similar. The Foundation has everything under control.
But when disaster strikes, this paradisal pocket dimension goes from unimportant to a potential evacuation point. Unfortunately, there's only space for about 100 000 people, so who stays and who goes?
There'll be a couple of main characters with differing opinions on whether to use this or not. When Paradise is filled however, the gateway shuts, and chaos ensues. Turns out the gateway was simply a way for a primordial nature spirit to gain sacrifices to increase its power and spread, and suddenly a new godlike entity enters the already chaotic battlefield of Earth.

Hook/Attention Grabber: While somewhat similar to SCP-778, this Paradise is in fact being freely offered and can be seen. I believe it is different enough from that SCP that it can be considered a completely seperate idea.
More importantly, this concept plays with human corruption, greed, desperation, and selflessness. Sometimes, stopping the bad people is easier than stopping the good.

Additional Notes: See my responses for more detail.

Anyway, thanks for reading!
